slice: M1 vertical slice - Day 1 (C1 complete) + Day 2 opening (C2 start)

evidence.name: The Burial Register Entry
evidence.description: St. Cynog's register, Josiah Vale: 'decline of years'. Dr Bellamy's hand, dated three days before the burial.
evidence.examine_detail: The ink is Bellamy's, but the phrasing is not a doctor's. 'Decline of years' for a man who walked the moor road weekly. Someone chose the words for him.
evidence.source: St. Cynog's churchyard - the open register

evidence.name: The Untouched Sin-Dish
evidence.description: The bread and salt plate found whole beside the boundary stone. A sin-eater's fee, refused.
evidence.examine_detail: The crust is dry but unbroken. Salt still crusted in the ring. No animal has touched it - even the crows keep away from this one. He set it down and walked away from his own rite.
evidence.source: Boundary stone Tŷ Uchel, the north road

evidence.name: The Register of Sins
evidence.description: Father's ledger, shut with seventeen cheap locks. The book the whole valley is afraid of.
evidence.examine_detail: Seventeen locks, each cheaper than the last - a farmer's padlocks, a saddle-lock, ahasp of bent nail. Locks bought one at a time, over years. The book was never meant to open again.
evidence.source: The sin-eater's cottage - under the engraving table

evidence.name: The Rite Paper
evidence.description: The sin-eating formula in Father's hand, with Welsh corrections in a second, older hand.
evidence.examine_detail: Bread, salt, and the spoken Welsh. The corrections are Nan Llewelyn's - he could not write the old words alone. The final line is crossed out and rewritten: the rite as this village performs it is not quite the rite of the books.
evidence.source: The sin-eater's cottage - the shelf above the hearth

evidence.name: The Torn First Page
evidence.description: A page torn from the ledger's beginning. The tear is old; the hiding is not.
evidence.examine_detail: Restored under charcoal and weight: a column of names begins - Nott, Coles, Prosser... and a marginal note in Father's hand: 'The bread stayed on the stone.'
evidence.source: The sin-eater's cottage - beneath the floor stone

evidence.name: Coles on the Last Months
evidence.description: The gravedigger's account: Josiah stopped answering the night calls this past spring.
evidence.examine_detail: A sworn shape, not a sworn statement: Coles will say it under the churchyard yew, not on paper. Still - he has no reason to lie about the man he buried.

evidence.name: Gwendolyn on the Paper of '39
evidence.description: The innkeeper's admission: a settlement paper with seventeen names exists, and hers is one of them.
evidence.examine_detail: She does not have the paper - 'the bank of the counter and the bottom of my heart' is where she keeps hers. But the count she gives is precise: seventeen guineas, seventeen names, one October night in 1839.

evidence.name: The Last Tray
evidence.description: Gwendolyn prepared Josiah's nightly brandy herself, four nights before his death. The bottle came by Griffiths' boy, with the doctor's blessing.
evidence.examine_detail: An ordinary kindness with an odd pedigree: the bottle's path ran Squire's agent, then doctor, then tray. She remembers the boy's gloves were too fine for a miner's son.

evidence.name: The Spring Sermon Line
evidence.description: Rev. Crane, since spring: 'This village dwells in sin.' Preached before any death, after he read the strangeness of the 1839 burial register.
evidence.examine_detail: A preacher's opinion - but the dating matters. He named the sickness months before the first man died of it, and he read the same register I now hold.

evidence.name: Coles' 'Hunger'
evidence.description: The gravedigger's whisper: 'It is the Hunger come back, mark me.' Folk fear, not fact.
evidence.examine_detail: The village's oldest story, worn smooth as a river stone: the shadow of sins uneaten. Useful to the frightened. Worthless to a magistrate.

evidence.name: The Restored List
evidence.description: The ledger's first page, restored: the names of 1839 in Josiah's iron hand, each beside a line of sin.
evidence.examine_detail: Nott - 'ate the orphan's bread.' Coles - 'the ring.' Prosser - 'the silenced bell.' And thirteen more lines the charcoal has not yet fully raised.

evidence.name: The Miller's Death - Scene Notes
evidence.description: Tobias Nott, dead across his own scale-board. Mouth packed with salt. My sketches and measurements of the mill floor.
evidence.examine_detail: No wound. Flour in his lungs from the struggle to breathe through the salt - he drowned in dry ground. The scale weights sit level; the man does not.
evidence.source: The mill on Afon Ddu - the floor

evidence.name: The Miller's Salt Sack
evidence.description: Coarse salt from the mill's own stores - the same grain that packed the dead man's mouth.
evidence.examine_detail: Bay salt, mill-bought, damp from the river air. The sack sits open by the door as if set down in haste - or in contempt.

evidence.name: The Tampered Weights
evidence.description: The mill's counter-weights: hollowed, packed with tallow. Every poorhouse sack weighed light for years.
evidence.examine_detail: Drilled from beneath, plugged with wax, blackened to match. Nott defrauded the poorest mouths in the parish - and the parish paid him in silence to keep doing it.

evidence.name: Prints by the Wheel-Race
evidence.description: Small, bare footprints in the river mud below the wheel. A child's size - or a slight woman's.
evidence.examine_detail: Heel-deep at the race's edge where only someone who knows the sluice would stand. The prints come from the water side and return to it. Not a ghost's path: a worker's.

evidence.name: Coles on the Miller's Fraud
evidence.description: The gravedigger carried the poorhouse sacks: 'Nott weighed light on the orphan's bread since the hunger years.'
evidence.examine_detail: He will not swear it - he carried the sacks, he did not read the scale. But Missus Hawke's winter count of the dead children makes the arithmetic for him.

link_rules.note: The witness saw the change in his habits; the plate proves the refusal. Object and testimony agree.
His own margin admits it: 'The bread stayed on the stone.'
A record sealed shut, and a ritualist who stopped answering the night calls. The last sin was never eaten.
Her paper and his page count the same seventeen names.
One rite bought for a whole village, one paper signed by seventeen hands.
Seventeen boxes the gravedigger nailed, and one long pit by the north wall - the page counts the same dead.
The first to die is the first name on the restored list.
Salt in the mouth of a man dead by bread-and-salt: the rite, inverted against its own sinner.
The miller's registered sin was eating the orphan's bread; his death was arranged as an accusation.
Consistent: the mouthful matches the mill's own stores. The source, not the hand.
Consistent: the tray was his nightly custom. Nothing more - yet.

link_rules.contradiction_reason: Folklore gives the Hunger no hands to leave a chosen thing untouched. Nothing establishes it exists at all.
The prints are human, small, and bare. Folklore gives the Hunger no feet.
Tampered weights are theft discovered; a sermon is an opinion about sin. One cannot weigh the other.

insights.name: A Refused Sin
insights.description: Josiah Vale died refusing to eat a final sin. The locked ledger, the untouched plate, and his broken habit of the night calls all say the same thing: someone asked, and he said no.

insights.name: The List of the Silence
insights.description: In 1839 this village paid seventeen guineas for seventeen signatures of silence. The ledger is the debt book of the drowned.

insights.name: The First Death Follows a Registered Sin
insights.description: Nott's death at the mill was staged as an accusation: salt in the mouth of the man whose registered sin was eating the orphan's bread. The register is being read aloud by someone - in flesh, not in spirit.
